1 BRIEF FACTS:
2. Briefly stated, it was the case of the complainant/FSO that samples of 'Mixed Fruit Jam' in sealed container were lifted by the Food Safety Officer from M/s. The Leela Palace (A unit of M/s. Leela Venture Ltd.), Diplomatic Enclave, New Delhi110023 for analysis under FSS Act on 29.05.2017, where the said food articles were found stored for serving or selling to the customers for human consumption.
The samples consisting of four sealed jars of 'Mixed Fruit Jam', each Jar containing 1 Kg taken as such in original condition bearing identical label declaration.

It was the case of the complainant/FSO that samples were divided into four equal parts by converting one sealed jar 'Mixed Fruit Jam' as one counter part of the sample and one counter part of the sample was sent to the Food Analyst for examination.

It appears that the no request was made by Food Business Operator to send 4th part of the sample for analysis from NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of the Food Safety &
Standars Rules, 2011 (for short 'FSSR'), and accordingly the counter parts of the samples in sealed packet as well as 4th counter part in separate packet were deposited with the designated officer on 30.05.2017.

The Food Analyst vide his report dated 07.06.2017 found that percentage of ingredients used i.e. mix fruits was not declared in the labels although the label emphasized through pictures, and therefore,
the sample was found to be misbranded for violation of regulation 2.2.2.2 (f) (i) of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling), 2011; and on the basis of said report, a complaint was filed before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM).
3.

10.0 The appellants have also contended that Delhi Food Laboratory in which the sample was analyzed and issued analytical report, is not legally competent lab to analyze the samples of food under FSS Act as per Section 43 of FSS Act; as the same is neither NABL Accredited nor notified in the Official Gazette as per provisions Section 3(1)(p) FSS Act.

PRESENT APPEAL:
7.

In the instant appeal, the impugned order dated 25.02.2022 is assailed inter alia on the grounds that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM), New Delhi District vide order dated 06.09.2018 had acquitted the appellant No.3 company without imposing Mr. Archit Aggarwal vs Shri Hukum Singh on 12 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192191821/
3 any penalty, which order had become final since the complainant did not file any appeal against the said order, and therefore, imposition of any penalty upon the appellant No.3 was in complete violation of law since remand of the case was not meant for fillingup any lacuna in the case of the complainant, for which reliance is placed on the decision in the case of MCD v. Kishan Chand & Ors., Criminal Appeal No. 122/72 dated 25.03.1975 decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

Adjudicating Officer (ADM) did not compel the Expert Food Analyst to appear in person for crossexamination despite an application moved by the applicants/appellants in this regard; and lastly that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM) has misinterpreted the advisory/directions issued by the FSSAI to issue improvement notice for rectification of minor label offences binding on the Commissioner Food Safety as per Section 16(5) of FSS Act.

Hence, relief is claimed to setaside the impugned order dated 25.02.2022.
8.

Notice of the present appeal was issued to the respondent and vide order dated 29.04.2022 the operation of the impugned order was stayed subject to furnishing of Demand Draft/FDR by the appellants to the extent of 50% of the amount of find imposed by the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM), which has been complied with.
The earlier order was modified on 28.10.2022 clarifying that demand draft in the sum of Rs. 80,000/ has been placed on the record by the appellants.
The respondent has opposed the appeal and has supported the legality of the impugned order.

DECISION:
9. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the rival parties.

I have also gone through the record of the present appeal and the previous order dated 01.04.2019 passed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Court (as her Ladyship was then) and the documents filed on the record.
I have also gone through the original record of the proceedings before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM), New Delhi District.
10. At the outset, I find no illegality, perversity or incorrect approach adopted by the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM) in passing the impugned order.

First thing first, in order to appreciate the present controversy raised by the appellants, it would be expedient to refer to the label on the product in question i.e. 'Mix Fruit Jam', the scanned copy of which is as under:

4 11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Secondly, the issue is whether there was any violation of 2.2.2.2(f)(i) of The Food Safety and Standards(Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards(Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It would be expedient to refer to the relevant Regulation, which provides as under:"2.2.2:
Labelling of Prepackaged Foods "In addition to the General Labelling requirements specified in 2.2.1 above every package of food shall carry the following information on the label, namely,.....
2. List of Ingredients:

Except for single ingredient foods, a list of ingredients shall be declared on the label in the following manner:--
.....
(b) The name of Ingredients used in the product shall be listed in descending order of their composition by weight or volume, as the case may be, at the time of its manufacture;
.....
(f) Every package of food sold as a mixture or combination shall disclose the percentage of the ingredient used at the time of the manufacture of the food (including compound ingredients or categories of ingredients),if such ingredient- (i) is emphasised as present on the label through words or pictures or graphics; or"
12. A careful perusal of the aforesaid Regulation visavis the scanned copy of the label would show that any food articles which is a combination or mixture of different fruits and sold in packaged form is required mandatorily to disclose the percentage of each ingredients at the time of manufacturing of such food article on the package,
particularly if such ingredient is emphasized by depicting on the label through words or pictures or graphics.

A bare perusal of the instant label would show that admittedly the label showed pictures of different fruits and other ingredients viz.
Cherry, Pineapple, Peer, Grapes etc. appearing on the package.

The aforesaid package of the sample food articles / mixed fruit jam admittedly failed to comply with the regulations in so far as it omitted to specify or mention the percentage of the ingredients used and there is no merit in the plea by the learned Counsel for the appellants that the sample were not examined by accredited Laboratory and the report dated 07.06.2017 of the Food Analyst cannot be taken into consideration since it was observed by the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM) that the alleged offence is relatable to the declaration on the label and there is not issue about its quality or standard and for that reason alone, the decision in the case of Pepsico India Holding Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector & Anr. (Supra) as also M/s. Nestle India Ltd. v. FSSAI (Supra) have no bearing bearing in this case.

5 13.

sentences.text: Thirdly, in so far as plea raised by the learned Counsel for the appellants that no liability had been imposed upon the respondent No.7 company i.e. M/s. Vidya Sagar Food Pvt. Ltd., the earlier order passed by the then Ld. District & Sessions Judge/Appellate Tribunal dated 01.04.2019 considered the entire gamut of the facts and circumstances and a careful perusal of the previous order dated 01.04.2019 would show that the matter was remanded back for a fresh adjudication so as to hear the parties and ascertain culpability of the respondent No.7 company, if any.
The ratio in the cited case of MCD v. Kishan Chand (supra) has no bearing in the instant matter since the facts in the cited case were distinguishable.

It was a case where alleged offence under Section 17 of the earlier enactment viz.
Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 were committed by the company and its Salesman and partner who were put to trial and the company had been acquitted by the trial court but the Salesman and partner were convicted, who assailed the conviction successfully in the appeal before the Ld. Sessions Judge and were accordingly acquitted; and the distinguishing feature is that no appeal against acquittal of the company had been filed by the complainant/MCD and it was in the said scenario that the acquittal of the company had become final and it was held that the partner could not be convicted.

At the cost of repetition, the narrative of the earlier Judgment dated 01.04.2019 clearly brings to the fore that the Ld. Appellate Tribunal/District & Sessions Judge found an illegality in the impugned order dated 06.09.2018 in as much as the respondent No.7/ company had been left out and the matter was remanded back for fresh consideration after hearing the parties.

Before parting with this case, a new plea was introduced that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM) failed to appreciate that as per Regulation 2.3.31 specifying ingredients for Jam, it is provided that produced shall be manufactured from not less than 45% by weight of original prepared fruit, exclusive of any added sugar or optional ingredients of finished product except where fruit is strawberry or raspberry where it shall contain not less than 25 % fruit.
I am afraid said plea is a new twist introduced by the learned Counsel for the appellants at the appeal stage, which was never argued before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM).

Moreover, the Regulation 2.3.31 is to be read in conjunction of Regulation 2.2.2.2 (f) (i) of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling), 2011 and there is no escape from the conclusion that the percentage of the ingredients used is mandatorily required to be depicted.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling), 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It goes without saying that advisory of FSSAI is mere an advisory and not biding that any improvement notice should have been issued.
14. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the present appeal is devoid of any merit and the same is dismissed.
The appellants are directed to comply with the impugned order dated 25.02.2022 passed by the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM) within 30 days as per law.

The appellants have deposited the 50% of the penalty and the bank draft dated 12.05.2022 drawn on Citi Bank, which was for the period of three months shall be revalidated by the appellant, which be returned to the appellants for revalidation and the penalty imposed be paid accordingly.
The interim order dated 29.04.2022 stands vacated.
15. Record of the Ld. ADM be returned along with copy of this judgment.
Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.

The appellants have deposited the 50% of the penalty and the bank draft dated 12.05.2022 drawn on Citi Bank, which was for the period of three months shall be revalidated by the appellant, which be returned to the appellants for revalidation and the penalty imposed be paid accordingly.
The interim order dated 29.04.2022 stands vacated.
15. Record of the Ld. ADM be returned along with copy of this judgment.
